subject: Discovery Recap: BrightCart — Embeddings & Reranking (index scale, latency targets)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@brightcart.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap — BrightCart: embeddings & reranking follow-up

Hi Elena — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we’re aligned.

Pain points you shared:
- Search relevance has degraded for long-tail and seasonal SKUs (high false negatives).
- Relevance tuning in Elasticsearch is brittle; you’re seeing frequent manual rule changes.
- Current latency and cost tradeoffs: product detail + rerank flow is adding 180–250ms on average which is hurting conversions.

Current stack we discussed:
- Embedding generator: third-party API (OpenAI today) for 1536-dim product embeddings.
- Vector DB: Pinecone (producer-tier), nightly batch upserts of product catalog.
- Fallback: Elasticsearch scoring for signal blending and filters.
- Index scale estimate: ~25M active product vectors today (you mentioned ~27M in the repo; see Elena’s note below).
- Query patterns: mix of single-item similarity and top-K rerank (typical rerank requests ask for top-50 then re-score offline). Peak traffic ~300 qps, baseline ~50–80 qps, heavy daytime spikes.

Success criteria you called out:
- Relevance improvement measurable via A/B (CTR, add-to-cart).
- p95 end-to-end rerank latency <= 150ms (target); p99 < 250ms.
- Cost per query target < $0.005 (or 40% improvement vs current).
- Pilot must be able to show reproducible gains on a ~1–5M sample index within 4–6 weeks.

What we recommended (high level):
- Pilot with Redwood on a 1–5M slice of your catalog to validate rerank quality and latency.
- Run model variants: full-fp model for quality baseline + quantized variant to meet latency/cost SLOs.
- Use Redwood’s prefix/KV cache for hot SKUs and workload-aware batching to tame tail latency during spikes.
- Instrument product-level evals and tie to mutual metrics (CTR / conversion).

Next steps / asks from your side:
1) Confirm index size (approx active vectors) and average embedding dim (you mentioned 1536).
2) Provide a short list of 2–3 example queries and a set of labelled relevance checks if available (we can run offline evals).
3) Are there any internal constraints (data residency, model families blocked, KMS requirements)?

We attached a short discovery deck and a draft mutual action plan to outline timelines and responsibilities.

Attachments: BrightCart-Discovery-Deck.pdf, BrightCart-Mutual-Action-Plan.xlsx

I’ll follow up with a proposed pilot timeline and pricing options tomorrow. Thanks again — excited to dig in.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear notes. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Index size: ~27M active product vectors (we counted product variants separately).
- Embedding dim: 1536, yes.
- Vector DB: Pinecone (we’re on standard plan today).
- We also maintain a realtime update stream into Elasticsearch for pricing/availability filters.

Latency / cost pressures: our product team is okay with a small increase in tail latency during tradeoffs, but the business target is p95 <= 150ms (end-to-end) for rerank requests that affect checkout flows. Cost target for infra margin on the rerank step is <$0.005 per query.

We can provide a small labelled relevance set (~250 queries) and a few sample logs for offline evals. I’ll ask the Search team to share those by EOD Wednesday.

Two asks from me:
- Pilot pricing options (1-month proof-of-value for 1–5M vectors; 3-month expanded pilot for 5–10M).
- Can Redwood guarantee a p95 SLO as a commercial offering for Dedicated or will that be an internal target only?

Happy to do a 30-min technical deep-dive with your engineering contact (copying Dylan here).

Regards,

Dylan’s notes / asks:

- Quantization: with 1536-dim vectors at 27M, we should test int8 and int4 quant variants to hit their p95 target. We’ll need a baseline quality test with full-precision to quantify delta.
- Batch patterns: they mentioned spikes to 300 qps — is that sustained or short bursts? If sustained, we need reserved capacity (Dedicated) pricing; if short bursts, caching + burst pools could be fine.
- Recommend that Marissa get their labeled set and a small sample of production logs (anonymized) — that will let us run offline rerank evals before spinning up infra.

I’ll join the technical deep-dive and can bring one of our infra engineers if we need kernel-level perf numbers.
